question: What is the best compromise (ΓΩMean) in the BeCoMe method?
expected_facts: the best compromise is the average of the arithmetic mean and the median
each component (lower, peak, upper) is averaged separately

question: Does a small Δmax mean the expert panel agreed?
expected_facts: a small Δmax does not mean the panel agreed
Δmax measures the distance between the mean and the median, not the panel's overall spread

question: What agreement percentage counts as high versus moderate?
expected_facts: the maximum error as a share of the scale width gives the label: up to 20 percent is High Confidence
up to 40 percent is Moderate
beyond 40 percent is Low
the label says how close the mean and the median are, not whether the experts agree

question: In the flood-prevention worked example, what were the arithmetic mean, median, and compromise centers?
expected_facts: the arithmetic mean's center is 20.28
the median's center is 8.33
the best compromise's center is 14.31
the maximum error is 5.97

question: In the five-manager budget example, what is the best compromise and the maximum error?
expected_facts: the best compromise is (5.50, 8.50, 13.00)
the maximum error is 0.00, meaning perfect agreement

question: If I widen my opinion's range but keep the same peak, does the group's compromise move?
expected_facts: widening an opinion by the same amount on both sides of the same peak does not move the centroid of the compromise
widening the range does not weaken the expert's vote

question: How do I express a crisp, fully certain opinion?
expected_facts: a crisp number enters the same value three times
lower equals peak equals upper, a triangle with no width

question: What is the formula for the centroid of a fuzzy triangular number?
expected_facts: the centroid Gx equals (A + C + B) divided by 3

question: Why doesn't one extreme opinion drag the median the way it drags the mean?
expected_facts: the median barely moves when one person takes an extreme position
the mean uses every opinion, which is both its virtue and its flaw

question: Which chart view do I see first when I open my project's results?
expected_facts: the landscape view is what opens by default
the centroid view collapses each opinion to a single point

question: We want to run a 'do we agree with this proposal or not' vote rather than estimate a quantity - can BeCoMe handle that kind of question in the app right now?

gold_sources.section: The agreement mode is not finished

expected_facts: the method has an agreement mode for 'should we' questions, but it is not usable in the app yet
it reads a 0 to 100 scale with no unit and rounds the compromise to one of five positions, from strongly disagree to strongly agree
the create-project form requires a unit, so such a project cannot be created

question: Kolik kroků vlastně projde výpočet BeCoMe, než dostanu finální výsledek?

gold_sources.section: The BeCoMe algorithm, step by step

expected_facts: the BeCoMe algorithm has five steps
the fifth and final step is a summary that lists the best compromise, the arithmetic mean, the median and the maximum error

question: Když si v grafu zapnu zobrazení jednotlivých názorů expertů, co mi to řekne o skupině navíc, co ta čtyři čísla neukážou?
expected_facts: it shows whether the panel is one group with some spread, or two groups with a gap between them
turning on Show individual opinions puts the grey triangles of the individual opinions behind the result

question: Hodí se BeCoMe na rozhodnutí typu 'vybereme dodavatele A, nebo dodavatele B'?
expected_facts: BeCoMe fits badly when the question is a choice between options rather than a quantity
it also fits badly when there is a right answer someone could look up, or when one person's judgment should win outright

question: Kolega mě prý pozval do projektu jako experta, ale žádnou pozvánku nikde nevidím. Čím to může být?
expected_facts: you must be signed in with the email address the invitation was created for
only someone who already has an account can be invited
an invitation is not sent by email: it appears in the Invitations tab

question: When I enter my low, most-likely, and high estimates for an opinion, does the app check that they're in the right order, or will it accept anything?
expected_facts: the three values must satisfy lower <= peak <= upper
the form refuses an opinion whose values are not in that order

question: If I download an export of everything BeCoMe has on me, will it show the invitations I've sent to other people, or just the ones I've received?
expected_facts: the export includes the invitations you received, not the ones you sent
sent invitations are left out because they are about the person you sent them to

question: In the case study about cross-border commuters during the pandemic, did the panel of officials generally lean toward allowing travel or restricting it?
expected_facts: the panel rates whether cross-border commuters should be allowed to travel on a Likert scale from 0 (strongly disagree) to 100 (strongly agree), so leaning toward disagreement means leaning against allowing travel
the panel leans toward disagreement: 14 of 22 answer 0 or 25
the Foreign Affairs role strongly supports travel (100), while the Interior and Defense roles oppose it (0)

question: For the flood-prevention example, is it fair to just say 'the answer is 14.31 percent' when I explain the result to someone?

gold_sources.section: What to say when you quote it

expected_facts: quoting 14.31 percent on its own implies a panel that broadly settled around fourteen, which it did not
only the economist's range contains 14.31; every other opinion sits in one of two camps
a fair statement says the panel split into two camps roughly 40 points apart

question: One backend test is failing and the parallel test output is too jumbled to read. How do I get pytest to run it without the parallel workers?
expected_facts: pass -n 0 to run pytest serially instead of in parallel
it is the way to read one failure closely, because the output of parallel workers interleaves

question: Když v BeCoMe zakládám nový projekt, k čemu slouží pole se škálou - je to už odhad výsledku, nebo něco jiného?
expected_facts: the scale sets the minimum, the maximum and the unit of the project's answer, for example 0 to 100 with unit %
the scale is the boundary every opinion has to fit inside, not a guess at the answer

question: Je moje heslo v BeCoMe uloženo tak, že by si ho teoreticky mohl někdo přečíst, třeba někdo s přístupem k databázi?
expected_facts: the password itself is never stored, only a bcrypt hash of it
the hash cannot be turned back into the password, and it is computed with a different salt for every account, so two people with the same password get different hashes

question: V té případové studii o rozpočtu na covid, které ministerstvo navrhlo vyšší podporu a které nižší?
expected_facts: the Interior role proposes higher support, 60-90 billion
the Education role proposes lower support, 15-60 billion, peaking at 40

question: Proč po mně aplikace při zadávání názoru chce rovnou tři čísla, a ne jen jedno konkrétní číslo?
expected_facts: a single number throws away the width of the expert's range, which says how confident they are
an expert who says 60 with a range of 40 to 80 and one who says 60 with a range of 58 to 62 have said different things, which a method averaging single numbers cannot tell apart

question: Do jakých tabulek se v databázi BeCoMe ukládají názory expertů a pozvánky do projektu?
expected_facts: expert opinions are stored in the expert_opinions table, unique per user and project
project invitations are stored in the invitations table, unique per project and invitee

question: Dá se nějak zjistit, jak moc by se změnil výsledný kompromis, kdyby se z panelu vyřadil názor jednoho konkrétního experta?
expected_facts: the sensitivity analysis chart lets you toggle individual experts on and off with checkboxes to see how their inclusion affects the final compromise
the chart recalculates in real time as you toggle an expert
this is in the visualization notebook run locally with Jupyter, not in the web application
